title: The six-vertex Mahler-type conjecture for centrally symmetric planar convex bodies
statement:
Let $B\in\mathcal{K}^2_o$ be an $o$-symmetric convex body in $\mathbb{R}^2$, let $Q_6(B)$ denote the associated six-vertex convex polygon, and let $B^{\circ}$ be the polar body of $B$. **Six-vertex Mahler-type conjecture.**

$$
\lambda_2(Q_6(B))\lambda_2(B^{\circ})\geq 8,
$$

with equality if $B$ is a parallelogram. This conjecture would imply that $m^{HT}(n,2)=\frac{8}{\pi}$ for all $n\geq 7$; the surrounding discussion presents it as an open question motivated by Mahler's planar volume-product inequality.
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.11496

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2025).
source_name: Z. Lángi and S. Wang, “Variants of a theorem of Macbeath in finite dimensional normed spaces”, arXiv:2507.11496 (2025).
